title: Oncall & Incident Response Playbook (Comprehensive)
author: Priya Shah
summary: This playbook documents Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response processes, runbook templates, postmortem expectations, rotation schedules, game day planning, and customer/status-page communication templates. It is the canonical reference for responders and service owners when an incident occurs.
introduction: Purpose: Provide a single, practical reference for responders and service owners to detect, respond to, communicate, and learn from incidents. Scope: Applies to all production services and customer-facing endpoints across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Goals: limit customer impact, restore service fast, and capture learnings to prevent recurrence.
incident_process:
Overview:
1) Detection & Triage
   - Alerts surface via PagerDuty, Logs (ELK), Metrics (Prometheus), and Synthetic tests.
   - Triage owner (on-call) acknowledges within 5 minutes for P1/P0.
2) Severity classification
   - P0 (Critical): Wide customer impact, data loss, security incident. Response within 5 minutes; page SRE/Eng leadership.
   - P1 (High): Major customer impact or key system outage; response within 15 minutes.
   - P2 (Medium): Degraded but usable; respond within 1 business hour.
   - P3 (Low): Minor issue, backlog.
3) Initial response steps (first 15 minutes for P0/P1)
   - Acknowledge and create an incident channel (Slack #inc-<service>-YYYYMMDD).
   - Record: incident_id, severity, owner, summary, detection signal, and affected customers.
   - Run the relevant runbook (see Runbooks section).
4) Mitigation & containment
   - Apply safe mitigations first (traffic blackholes, scale up, fallback model variants).
   - Prioritize customer-facing fixes over internal cleanup.
5) Communication
   - Post initial message to status.redwood.com and internal channel within 30 minutes for P0/P1. Use templates in Status Page & Comms section.
6) Resolution & Recovery
   - Verify end-to-end recovery and monitor for regressions for 30-60 minutes.
7) Post-incident
   - Create a postmortem within 72 hours (see Postmortem Process).
Ownership: incident commander (IC), primary responder, secondary/backup, and customer success liaison for customer impact.
runbooks:
Runbook standards:
- Every critical service must have a runbook with: scope, pre-reqs, runbook steps, rollback steps, safety checks, contact list, and dashboard links.
- Runbooks are executable playbooks: short commands, exact dashboards, and clear decision points.
Runbook template (short):
- title: One-line description
- scope: Which hosts/endpoints/customers
- pre-reqs: access, run-as, environment variables
- detection: alert names and metrics thresholds
- mitigation steps (1..n): exact CLI/API commands, expected outcomes
- rollback: how to revert any mitigation
- validation: queries and checks to confirm success
- post-actions: PR, postmortem, follow-up tickets
Example: Realtime API 503 runbook (excerpt)
1) Confirm alert: grafana dashboard > API error rate > 5% over 5m.
2) Check upstream model pool health: curl --silent "https://internal-api/v1/pool/health" | jq .status
3) If pool unhealthy: restart pool worker: kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/pool-worker-<pool-id>
4) If restart fails or errors persist, scale up dedicated replica set: kubectl -n inference scale deployment/pool-worker-<pool-id> --replicas=<replicas+2>
5) If traffic routing issue suspected: revert recent routing changes via gitops revert of infra/ingress-config
6) Post initial message to channel and update status page using template.
Runbook ownership: team, owner, last_reviewed date. Minimum review cadence: quarterly for critical runbooks.
postmortem_process:
Objectives: capture timeline, root cause, impact, communication timeline, corrective actions with owners and due dates.
Timing & ownership:
- Draft created by IC within 72 hours.
- Technical lead completes timeline and root cause within 7 days.
- Review and publish within 14 days.
Postmortem template (required fields):
- title
- incident_id
- severity
- summary (one-paragraph)
- timeline (minute-granular for first hour, then 5-15 minute buckets)
- impact (customers, internal SLOs, revenue exposure)
- root cause analysis (what failed and why)
- corrective actions (owner, type: remediation/prevention, due date)
- lessons learned
- follow-ups (PRs, infra changes, runbook updates)
Quality expectations:
- No blame: factual, evidence-backed analysis.
- Postmortem review: SRE + service owners + product + customer success (if customers impacted).
- Track actions in Jira and verify completion at 30/60/90 day snapshots.
Severe incidents (security/data loss) require legal and security review and may be marked "restricted" and redacted for public distribution.
oncall_rotations:
Roles:
- Primary responder (pager duty): first responder and triage.
- Secondary (backup): supports and takes over if primary unavailable.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates the response for P0/P1 until stability.
- Ops/SRE support: handles infra ops (scaling, rollouts).
- Customer Success liaison: handles customer comms and escalations.
Rotation rules:
- Typical rotation cadence: 1-week primary shifts for product/SRE engineers.
- Night/weekend rotations: 2-week shifts for distributed coverage.
- Handover: every shift must include a 15-minute overlap for knowledge transfer and outstanding issues.
Escalation matrix (summary):
- Pager triggers -> Primary -> 10 minutes -> Secondary -> 15 minutes -> SRE Lead -> 30 minutes -> Eng Director -> Exec on-call.
On-call expectations and etiquette:
- Acknowledge within defined SLOs (5m for P0).
- Maintain status in the incident channel and update status page.
- Respect on-call balance: limit meeting loads during active on-call week and provide on-call compensatory time off.
On-call tooling and contacts:
- PagerDuty for paging and escalation policies.
- Slack incident channels auto-created via PagerDuty integration.
- Runbook links pinned to channel.
- Phone escalation numbers stored in the secure Vault (secrets-managed).
game_days:
Purpose: validate runbooks, test escalation, surface gaps in tooling and runbook accuracy.
Cadence: at least two game days per quarter across infra, serving runtime, and API teams.
Scope & scenarios:
- Scenario A: Sudden cluster-wide model pool failure (model-serving fallback).
- Scenario B: High error-rate from upstream dependency (third-party auth service).
- Scenario C: Latency spike under synthetic load (autoscaling & batching).
Planning checklist:
1) Define scenario, objectives, and success criteria.
2) Schedule: announce 2 weeks in advance; optional seatings for observers.
3) Create a safe, reversible fault injection plan (prefer staging but limited safe production experiments allowed with approvals).
4) Post-game-day: run a mini-postmortem, capture action items, and update runbooks.
Typical agenda (2 hours):
- 00:00-00:15: kickoff & goals
- 00:15-00:60: inject fault & live response
- 00:60-01:15: recovery & validation
- 01:15-02:00: retrospective & action item capture
Deliverables: runbook updates, Jira tickets for tooling gaps, and a short write-up posted to the Confluence game-day page.
status_page_and_comms_templates:
Status page and comms templates (use for all customer-facing incidents)
1) Initial public status (short):
- Title: Degraded service for <service-name>
- Impact: Customers may experience increased latency and HTTP 5xx errors on <endpoints>.
- Current status: Investigating.
- Next update: In 30 minutes.
- Mitigation: Routing to fallback model variant.
Internal incident channel initial message (Slack):
- :rotating_light: Incident: <INCIDENT_ID>
- Severity: P1
- Summary: Increased 5xx from realtime-api since 12:42 UTC, likely model pool exhaustion.
- IC: @<name> (contact: pager)
- Actions in progress: scaling pool, restarting workers, updating status page.
Progress update template (public):
- Title: Update — <service-name> degraded — mitigation in progress
- Body: We have implemented temporary routing changes and are seeing partial recovery. Error rate down from 14% to 6% in the last 15 minutes. Next update in 15-30 minutes.
Resolved message (public):
- Title: Resolved — <service-name> incident
- Body: The issue affecting <service-name> has been resolved as of <time>. Root cause analysis and follow-ups will be posted within 14 days.
Customer outreach template (for impacted customers):
- Subject: Incident <INCIDENT_ID> — temporary service degradation
- Body: Brief description of impact, timeframe, current mitigation, and a contact (CS liaison). For high-severity customers include a dedicated follow-up call offer and link to postmortem when published.
Communication rules:
- Publish a public status for P1/P0 within 30 minutes.
- Do not speculate; provide facts and tactical mitigation steps.
- Coordinate all customer-facing statements with CS and Legal for P0/security incidents.
sla_and_slos:
Relevant SLOs for on-call & incident response:
- API availability (hosted realtime endpoints): 99.9% monthly (SLO).
- API p99 latency: < 600ms for production hosted tier.
- Error rate SLO: HTTP 5xx < 0.5% rolling 7d for production.
Alert thresholds (examples):
- P0: Availability drop > 5% points over 5 minutes or data loss detected.
- P1: Error rate > 3% for 10 minutes or p99 latency > 2x target for 15 minutes.
- P2: Error rate > 1% for 30 minutes.
SLO burn policy:
- If SLO burn rate exceeds 5x expected within a 24-hour window, escalate to SRE lead and notify product leadership.
- Track SLOs in the dashboards and include SLO status in postmortem impact section.
ownership_and_escalation:
Team ownership model:
- Service owner (team) is responsible for runbook accuracy and post-incident remediation.
- SRE is responsible for on-call tooling, escalation policy, and capacity-related mitigations.
- Customer Success handles external escalation and customer comms.
Escalation contact summary:
- PagerDuty -> Primary responder -> Secondary -> SRE Lead -> Prod Eng Manager -> Director of Engineering -> Executive on-call.
- For security incidents: PagerDuty tags escalate to Security On-Call and Legal automatically.
Contact resources:
- On-call roster: https://redwood.internal/roster (restricted)
- Pager: https://pagerduty.com/teams/redwood
- Incident runbooks index: https://confluence.redwood/incoming/oncall-runbooks (internal link)
